To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phosphatase and kinase properties of PP2A and CAMKII, respectively, form a bistable switch that is responsible for the induction of LTP and that this bistable switch is coupled to a second bistable switch, the kinase switch, that maintains LTP.
the coupled CaMKII and PP2A switches can form a tristability that can explain the experimental findings regarding LTP and LTD.
the properties of the CaMKII and PP2A switches can lead to a trisatble biochemical switch that can explain the bistability required for the maintenance of LTP and LTD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biochemical mechanisms that produce long-term changes in synaptic strength.
the mechanisms underlying the bidirectional plasticity of individual synapses.
understanding how the properties of the individual proteins in a biochemical network can lead to complex behaviors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CaMKII and PP2A switches, together with a third switch that has not yet been identified, form a tristability that underlies LTP and LTD.
a coupled phosphatase and kinase switch is a minimal model of a synapse, which can explain LTP and LTD.
a coupled phosphatase and kinase switch is required to produce the tristability necessary to explain the experimental data on long-term synaptic plasticity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a coupled phosphatase and kinase switch produces the tristability required for LTP and LTD.
the coupled PP1 and CaMKII bistable switches can be combined with the CaMKII-PP2A tristable switch to provide a minimal model of a synapse that can be bidirectionaly modified.
the coupled phosphatase and kinase switch can produce the tristability required for long-term potentiation and long-term depression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bistability of the kinase switch is not sufficient to explain LTP and LTD.
tristability, rather than bistability, is required for the persistent modification of synapses.
the tristability is achieved by the interplay between a kinase and a phosphatase.
